title: Orthokeratology and Low-Intensity Laser Therapy for Slowing the Progression of Myopia in Children

groups.description: single-vision distance spectacles worn the entire day; 74 completers of 100 randomised; Nanchang University Affiliated Eye Hospital, Nanchang, China
overnight orthokeratology (Euclid Systems Ortho-k), at least 7 consecutive hours nightly; 81 completers of 100 randomised; Nanchang, China
low-level laser therapy ('LILI' in the tables): 650 nm, 2 ± 0.5 mW, twice daily for 3 minutes, with single-vision distance spectacles; 74 completers of 100 randomised; Nanchang, China

exclusions.what: Table 3 'Change in AL (mm)' at 1, 3 and 6 months
exclusions.reason: change series of the same groups; the absolute series of Table 2 is used when both are given
baseline axial length duplicated by the Table 2 baseline row, which is cited instead

exclusions.what: F main-effect and crossover-effect rows of Table 2; F and p columns of Tables 1 and 3
exclusions.reason: test statistics and p-values are not admissible

exclusions.what: SER and SFChT blocks of Tables 1-3
exclusions.reason: refraction and choroidal thickness are not axial length (protocol inclusion 1)
model estimates are not admissible and are not tabulated values

notes: 300 children randomly assigned to control, orthokeratology or low-level laser therapy (100 each); 229 completed the 6-month study (control 74, OK 81, LLLT 74) and are tabulated; the tabulated sets are at least 70% of the randomised groups (protocol inclusion 5), so they are admitted.
Only left eyes were analysed (one eye per child), used as tabulated (protocol inclusion 7).
Visits at baseline, 1, 3 and 6 months; axial length device named only by manufacturer (Carl Zeiss Meditec), recorded as unstated.
The low-level laser (650 nm red light, 2 mW, twice daily) is classified as repeated low-level red-light therapy (red_light).
Subfoveal choroidal thickness and spherical equivalent refraction are tabulated (Tables 1-3), not extracted.
